mbm-2551.clue: The red disc has its own seat.
mbm-2551.quote: My dog used to chase every frisbee I threw until I gave her the red one. Now she sits on it under the picnic bench and watches our whole game like a landlord.

mbm-2552.clue: I keep my whistle on a green string.
mbm-2552.quote: We tied our raft crew's whistles with different colors. At the calm stretch we hung our life jackets on one branch to dry. The riverbank looked like a tree growing bright little birds.

mbm-2553.clue: My golf glove has a small green island.
mbm-2553.quote: I missed the fairway and found my ball beside one perfect tuft of moss. I sketched the shape on my glove. When I'm nervous over a putt I look down and find that soft landing spot.

mbm-2554.clue: I play the yellow tower backward.
mbm-2554.quote: Our board game lost its direction arrow. I carved a little wooden chimney that points the way when you turn it. The rest of the village watches the yellow tower for the wind.

mbm-2555.clue: My sleeping bag smells like an orange grove.
mbm-2555.quote: Dad put orange peel in the tent to sweeten the air. I found a dry strip in my bag three months later. One cold night at home it took me straight back to the ridge.

mbm-2556.clue: I make a map of the misses.
mbm-2556.quote: After every round I put a small dot where a stray ball took me. The useful part of my golf notebook is a map of blackberry bushes that nobody on the fairway ever sees.

mbm-2557.quote: I made a picnic quilt with dark triangles at the corners so we could stake it down in damp grass. My friends use those triangles as bases for games before lunch.

mbm-2558.clue: I needed four kitchen chairs to show Dad what I’d finished.
mbm-2558.quote: I kept count of the embroidered border on my pollera with a long strip of squared paper, one red dot for each repeat. Dad folded it like an accordion. When the border was done, he lined up four chairs so we could open the paper all the way.

mbm-2559.clue: The monsters on our shelf have very small teeth.
mbm-2559.quote: Our anime club makes paper models while we watch. I forgot to leave tabs on my monster's jaw. Gran lent me her pinking shears and gave him the tidiest little grin in town.

mbm-2560.clue: I made the rain a little quieter for Mum.
mbm-2560.quote: The lid on the rain barrel outside Mum’s window knocked all night. I quilted a padded cap from her old garden apron and tied it on. Next shower we opened the window and listened to the water for the first time in ages.

mbm-2561.clue: I take the summit home on my shoelace.
mbm-2561.quote: I tie a different knot at the end of every trail. My brother can tell which ridge I walked by looking at my boots. Rain makes the longest hikes a challenge to untie.

mbm-2562.clue: I see the first trailer from the doorway.
mbm-2562.quote: I like the moment when daylight is still behind me and the movie screen glows ahead. My friend saves the aisle seat so I can enjoy that half-second every Friday.

mbm-2563.clue: I taught my computer to lose at checkers politely.
mbm-2563.quote: The little program I wrote used to clear the board when it lost. I drew a tiny pixel hand that tips its hat instead. Grandad comes over just to beat it now.

mbm-2564.clue: My lantern has a moth census.
mbm-2564.quote: I dot a page for every different moth that lands on our camp lantern. Last trip my daughter drew one enormous dot for herself because she'd spent just as long watching the light.

mbm-2565.clue: I write my last line on a paper boat.
mbm-2565.quote: When I finish a story I fold a copy of the final sentence into a little boat. My desk drawer holds a whole fleet. The one with the coffee ring is still my favorite ending.

mbm-2566.clue: I take the spare rope to supper.
mbm-2566.quote: I tied our sagging volleyball net with a length of bright blue rope. At sunset we used the rest as a handle for the picnic basket. Nothing on our beach works only one shift.

mbm-2567.clue: I keep two scores in my mint tin.
mbm-2567.quote: I carry two pieces of scoreboard chalk to beach volleyball in my old mint tin. One is for our match and one is for the kids keeping score by the net. Their side gives six points for a dive and an extra for shouting. I always check their score first.

mbm-2568.clue: I know one aircraft by its socks.
mbm-2568.quote: The owner of a little yellow plane hangs striped windsocks from the hangar roof. I sketch the plane and both socks in my notebook. They tell me which way the afternoon was blowing.

mbm-2569.clue: My crown has an elastic from the post office.
mbm-2569.quote: The king's crown fell over my ears in rehearsal. Our mail carrier gave me a thick red rubber band. From the front I was royalty. From the back my crown was registered post.

mbm-2570.clue: I write the first number very small.
mbm-2570.quote: I put my first deadlift number in a tiny square on our gym chalkboard. When new numbers go up there is always enough room for the one that got me through the door.

mbm-2571.clue: I bowl one frame for my old street.
mbm-2571.quote: The man who ran our corner shop taught me to bowl. I use his old pencil for frame seven. The eraser is gone, so all of those scores are strictly final.

mbm-2572.clue: The mat has one patch of sunshine.
mbm-2572.quote: I practice my form slowly enough to watch the dojo's window light cross the mat. I finish with my feet in the warm square. On rainy days I can still find the spot.

mbm-2573.clue: My palette has a butter compartment.
mbm-2573.quote: I paint with an old metal lunch tray. The little square where the butter went holds my brightest yellow. My niece calls every sunrise I paint toast.

mbm-2574.clue: I stitched the echo in green.
mbm-2574.quote: My sister hummed the same line each time we sewed a row. I ran one green stitch out of line every time she changed the tune. There's a waltz you can follow across the blanket with your finger.

mbm-2575.clue: I give every chapter its own teacup.
mbm-2575.quote: When I read a long book I rotate through the cups in the cupboard. The storm chapter got the chipped blue one. I still can't pick it up without hearing the rain.
